correctness.rationale: For a Garsia-unit function f in L², choose a common Lebesgue point ζ for f and |f|². Nontangential Poisson convergence yields Vf(z)=P|f|²−|Pf|²→0 in each Stolz cone at ζ. For a=rζ the disk-algebra function g_a=b_a+a has Poisson variance 1−|b_a|², norm exactly one, and its ε-superlevel sets are images of bounded pseudohyperbolic disks lying uniformly inside a Stolz cone tending to ζ. Hence Δ_r=sup_z min(Vf,Vg_a)→0. Centered Poisson L² triangle inequality gives ||f±g_a||_G<=1+sqrt(Δ_r), while both ||f|| and ||g_a|| equal one. Thus unit perturbations make both signed norms tend to one, contradicting strong extremity for every boundary point in all four spaces. No unsupported norm equivalence is used; analytic g_a belong to all four. Source checks/check_geometry.py inspected and the localization/Möbius algebra was independently reconstructed; finite sample checks are not proof for arbitrary f.
residual_risks: Relies on standard a.e. nontangential convergence for Poisson integrals of f and |f|²; does not establish uniform convergence rates over unit sphere.
Ordinary extreme points may exist and do not contradict non-strong extremity; result is norm-specific.

originality.rationale: Dyakonov 2026 explicitly raises the strongly extreme Garsia ball question in Section 2 without resolving it; his 2025 Theorem 2.7 / Corollary 2.8 classify ordinary extreme points and make the VMO phenomenon particularly notable. For BMO-type arc-average norms and H-infinity sup norms, strong extremity differs from the Poisson-variance Garsia norm. The submitted construction answers the exact stated strongly extreme variant and is not a corollary of the earlier ordinary extreme statements.
